operations.control: Loop/black_box or volatile sink control; do not subtract blindly.
operations.init: Construct rules state and run setup; parameter/model construction excluded.
operations.copy: Rust exact state clone; Java public full-state copy, which branches future chance RNGs and includes framework bookkeeping.
operations.observe: Owned permitted observation in Rust; player copy in Java.
operations.actions: Available actions on the prepared state.
operations.offered: Rust offered actions from a previously prepared observation.
operations.transition: Clone prepared state, then apply its first legal action; clone is INCLUDED.
operations.query: Next player/current actor, player result and score queries.
operations.fork: Rust observation-derived simulation fork; Java player copy/determinization. Semantics differ in stochastic games.
operations.encode: Rust permitted metadata/action/mask encoding with no named numeric payloads; full arrays measured through Python separately.
operations.save: Extract sufficient state data and serialize JSON; not a complete session file.
operations.load: Deserialize sufficient state JSON and validate/restore state.
operations.first: Rust FirstAvailableAgent; Java first-list-element baseline, not an added Java agent implementation.
operations.random: Select a prepared choice with the agent RNG.
operations.osla: Construct seeded OSLA and choose; Java includes player-copy input creation; heuristics/ties differ.
operations.mcts: Search at 32 iterations, rollout limit 4; algorithms/heuristics differ. Not a language ratio.
operations.game: Complete Random games through the uniform agent interface: actions from live state, observation/player-copy construction and actual Random agent selection in both engines. Blocks cover 32 fixed agent seeds (seed..seed+31). Includes setup; rule/trajectory differences remain.
operations.retain_states: Retain 1, 128 or 2048 exact prepared-state copies; sample initialized process baseline and loaded process.
operations.game_direct: Diagnostic full games with direct uniform index choice, omitting observation construction in both engines. Same 32-seed cycle as game; not the normal agent interface.
operations.game_aligned: Two-player Love Letter game with both winning-token targets set to six through Java's public parameter; otherwise the normal game path.
operations.game_aligned_direct: Aligned six-token Love Letter with direct choice and no observation construction.
operations.validate: Prepared legal-list enumeration and membership check; not every internal game validation instruction in isolation.
operations.apply: Checked in-place transition on inputs copied before each block timer; includes legality checks and automatic rule consequences.
operations.apply_control: Clock/loop floor for the prepared transition harness, 1000 blocks of 32 calls; never subtracted.
operations.history_copy: Love Letter retained current/last-round public/private knowledge buffers in Rust, action/text history lists in Java; differing contents and copy depth.

comparison_classes.matched_recorded_board_corpus: Existing validated 32 complete games per placement game, all recorded prefixes; same terminal boards/results/actions verified before timing.
comparison_classes.equivalent_initial_board_api: Both placement games at the same empty default board: init/copy/observe/actions/transition/query/first/random. Includes public API/storage differences; RNG implementations differ.
comparison_classes.semantic_difference: Stochastic rules/knowledge/trajectories and OSLA/MCTS algorithms differ. Ratios, where shown, describe measured implementations/fixtures and are not equal-work language multipliers.
comparison_classes.rust_only: Numeric encoding, persistence, Python transfer/grouping, portable models, external neural evaluation and browser-adapter workloads; no equivalent Java adapter/model implementation is assumed.

agent_coverage.first_available: All profiles; native and native browser-adapter probes.
agent_coverage.random: All profiles; prepared decisions and complete games.
agent_coverage.osla: Deterministic native placement OSLA; R=1 sampled native OSLA for stochastic games. Public Java OSLA measured separately.
agent_coverage.external_osla: Both placement games: Rust heuristic backend, Python heuristic backend, PyTorch observer-value backend, and grouped Python scoring.
agent_coverage.native_mcts: All profiles in Rust and Java with algorithm differences disclosed; Python and browser-adapter entry points also measured.
agent_coverage.neural_mcts: All profiles: Python/PyTorch independent trees, and local Rust inference through the native browser adapter. No Java neural baseline.
agent_coverage.local_neural_osla: Both placement games only; discounted observer-value model is separate from the full-vector MCTS model.
agent_coverage.q_table: Default Tic-Tac-Toe only, using the bundled test fixture; other games unsupported by this table example.

measurement_limits: Java and Rust seeds do not produce matching stochastic trajectories.
Cant Stop has approved action/rule differences; Love Letter has different 2-player winning-token threshold and tie/knowledge behavior.
OSLA heuristics/tie handling and MCTS traversal/expansion/evaluation differ; equal iteration limits are not identical search work.
The existing Java build/classpath is reused in its disposable writable workspace; the public reference stays untouched.
No new Java implementation, listener registry, decorator or neural backend is added for a benchmark.
Low-level probes take resolved integer seeds; run.py supports an integer or auto and records the resolved value.
Performance fixtures are deliberately seeded; small untrained neural models measure execution, not playing strength.

Public Java AbstractGameState.copy branches future RNGs using an internally unseeded stream; LoveLetterGameState also has a time-seeded redeterminization RNG. Setup/agent seed 42 does not make those Java search trajectories reproducible. The baseline is preserved; any displayed ratio is an observed fixture ratio, not an equal-work language comparison.

adapter_operations.fork: One fork of a separately imported prepared session; preparation/destruction excluded. Five batches of 16 independent sessions per process.
adapter_operations.fork_and_continue: The same fork plus one accepted First Available move through the native protocol.
adapter_operations.history: Export/import at actual cursors capped by termination, including controller/history validation.
